title: Sales and Trading (S&T) Explained
transcript: sales and trading sales and trading is a group at an investment bank consisting of salespeople and traders salespeople are people who call institutional investors like large funds and pitch investment ideas and opportunities traders are people who execute orders and advise clients on their financial positions both of these are the lifeblood that makes or breaks an investment securities firm the most important thing for these firms is to be able to sell services to clients and trade well in order to keep its clients the sales group works on many different types of activities that communicate information about securities to investors such as large institutions or individuals they also monitor investment news like earnings reports or M&A information additionally the sales group serves as an important function in initial public offerings for the investment bank since they need to sell the required number of shares in the secondary market for an IPO another important function of the sales group is that they develop relationships with investors and keep in contact with portfolio managers to get timely market information let's look at sales with respect to mutual funds exchange-traded funds and hedge funds investment firms that offer mutual funds and exchange-traded funds don't under I POS but instead make their money through fees from investing these firms need to employ effective sales staff to attract clients to their firm because the fees they earn are based on a percentage of money invested in the funds they offer thus more clients equals more investment capital equals more fees earned and thus meaning a higher profit for hedge funds investment sales can change depending on who does the selling and who they are selling to investment sales depend heavily on the hedge fund managers trading strategies and portfolio mix a hedge fund manager operates as a trader and could even be the only salesperson if it is a new fund hedge funds target both institutional investors and high-net-worth individuals ultimately sales work is closely intertwined with trading work no matter what type of firm you are act the bottom line of a salesperson is to convince potential investors that their firms traders are better than others for example a stockbroker tries to convince investors that the brokerage firm has better research and analysis in trading a hedge fund manager tries to convince investors that they can generate higher returns and sales people try to pitch the bank's ability to obtain the most capital for an IPO and deliver the most efficient buying and selling services for institutional investors we've looked at what the sales group does now let's look at the trading group the trading group buys and sell securities on behalf of their clients specializing in different investment areas this means that individual traders might be assigned to trade only the gold market or a specific market sector such as health care or transportation the trading group is responsible for managing both risk and capital and security analysis finally most traders and large firms engage in sales and trading with traders and other investment firms due to the large volume of securities being traded there are two basic types of trading agency trading and proprietary trading in agency trading traders act as the agent for clients and try to execute trades as skillfully as possible traders need to spread out their transactions when buying a large volume of shares at a good price to avoid driving up the price in proprietary trading traders trade using the financial firms own money for example a proprietary trader at a commercial bank might trade in the foreign exchange market to maximize the bank's capital proprietary traders usually have more freedom but are still restricted by the risk limits of the investment firm there's actually a third type of trader which is a flow trader that acts as a hybrid of both types for example a flow trader could be buying shares on behalf of a client but selling the client shares that are owned by the investment firm traders also trade different types of securities basic securities can be broken down into fixed income equities commodities and foreign exchange within each basic group of securities traders can become even further specialized for example fixed income traders can specialize in corporate bonds government bonds and other debt related instruments as well as different maturity times then there are financial derivatives such as collateralized debt obligations and contracts for difference which expand the categories of trading these have somewhat blurred the lines between categories for example collateralized debt obligations may be traded by traders who specialized in fixed income or those who specialized in derivatives in equity trading research teams and investment firms collect information about the companies they are tracking the financial health and position of those companies are then analyzed using metrics like ratio and DCF analysis investment firms can also expand this analysis by looking at the company's position in the market and industry as well as evaluating their management team this information is then given to the trading team when trading equities the equity trading group will usually have traders assigned to specifically trade stock indexes like the S&P 500 index there will also be agency traders who strictly act on behalf of clients these traders will usually trade a wide range of equities proprietary traders on the other hand are assigned to trade specific market sectors when it comes to trading commodities currencies options and everything else proprietary traders are typically very specialized there are commodity traders who are assigned to trade groups of commodity futures like precious metals and energy futures within each category traders can also specialize in a specific market then there are currency traders who specialize in trading one currency against others for example someone specializing in trading the British Pound will trade currency pairs like the pound against the US dollar finally options traders cover a wide range of trading and may fall into different trading groups like fixed income or equities based on the nature of the options sales and trading is a very lucrative career with great compensation to back it up however the competition for this field is fierce and requires talent and tons of effort to succeed the workload for a career in sales in trading involves long hours to succeed in sales you need to be confident and outgoing you need to be able to take initiative and have the motivation and drive to accomplish your goals you will need to be able to have a talent for pitching ideas and selling products as well as good knowledgeable and investment instruments you will also need to have a strong basis in financial analysis to succeed in trading you need to be able to handle stress and make quick decisions a trader also needs to have confidence in their decisions and enjoy doing research you will need to be able to identify and analyze investment opportunities as well as execute trades to minimize risk while maximizing profits if you want to check out more career resources and find out what finance jobs are best for you make sure to check out see FIS career map at corporate finance Institute comm we hope this video was helpful for you as an introduction to sales and trading
